content.text:
I'm escalating case B-016 to Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD). The business is in crypto, a restricted industry, and its state licence has not been verified.

**What sets the outcome**
- **Industry (5.2, 5.3):** The business is in crypto (virtual currency), which is restricted, so it goes to escalation. The exception for licensed businesses (5.3) doesn't apply because the licence is not verified.
- **Stale registry filing (3.5):** The registry filing is dated 2025-06-19. At review on 2026-10-27 it is about 16 months old, more than the 6-month limit. On its own this would mean requesting documents. Under 2.1 the more severe outcome wins, so the case is escalated.

**What passed**
- **Ownership is complete.** Directly, Rosa Ishikawa holds 20%, Iris Holdings LLC 46%, Wen Ishikawa 22% and Umar Ueda 12%, which adds up to 100%. Iris Holdings is owned 76% by Nora Eriksen and 24% by Tara Castillo. That gives Nora about 35% indirectly and Tara about 11%. Nora is the only person at 25% or more.
- **Control person and ID checks pass.** The control person is Rosa Ishikawa, the Chief Executive Officer. Her identity and Nora's are verified, and so are those of the other three people the system screened.
- **Other screening is clear.** No sanctions matches and no politically exposed persons were found. The business and every person screened are located in the US.

**Adverse media note**
Wen Ishikawa has an adverse media hit. At 22% ownership Wen isn't someone the procedure requires us to identify. The file also says only "yes", so we can't tell whether the report meets the 4.4 materiality test. That test needs a name match plus one other identifier, and a qualifying source. The hit doesn't change the outcome, but EDD may want to look at it.

The escalation needs no further facts.
